title: Lightweight Multimodal Deep Learning Framework for Cerebellar Ataxia Detection Using an MLP Encoder and Hybrid Optimizer
abstract: Background Cerebellar ataxia is characterized by abnormalities in gait, speech, ocular movement, and coordination, making accurate detection challenging. Purpose This study develops a lightweight multimodal Deep Learning (DL)-based framework for cerebellar ataxia detection. Research Design The proposed approach integrates voice, gaze, and body pose features from independent public datasets and performs class-level multimodal feature fusion to capture complementary motor and behavioral cues. Fine-grained features such as Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) and vocal perturbation measures, gaze fixation dynamics, and spatiotemporal body pose features are extracted using Python-compatible tools. Each modality is processed with a specific Multilayer Perceptron (MLP)-based encoder to produce small embeddings, which are fused through feature concatenation and processed by a fully connected MLP classifier. To ensure stable convergence and robust generalization capability on limited and noisy clinical data, a novel hybrid optimizer, Adaptive Sharp-Lookahead Lite, is used. Results Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 99.56% in distinguishing ataxia from normal cases under the adopted experimental setting. Conclusions The findings demonstrate the potential of the framework as a lightweight AI-based screening approach for resource-constrained settings.
